findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous: different (name, folder) pairs map to the same key
findings.body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` joins `name` and `parent` with `_`, and dashboard/folder UIDs may themselves contain `_`. A denial for dashboard `a` in folder `b_c` produces `ns.perm_<uid>_dashboards:read_a_b_c`, the same key as dashboard `a_b` in folder `c`. Check reads the denial cache first (`service.go:116-121`) and returns `Allowed: false` without looking at permissions, so the second dashboard is silently denied for up to `shortCacheTTL` even when the user can access it. The key also leaves out the identity type (`checkReq.IdentityType`). Subjects of different types that share a UID string (for example the anonymous or renderer subject and a user) share denial entries, even though `getIdentityPermissions` resolves their permissions differently (`service.go:330-339`). Fix: use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or encode the fields (length-prefix or escape them), and add the identity type to the key.

findings.title: Every first-time denial now runs a full permission DB query
findings.body: `getUserPermissions` and `getAnonymousPermissions` no longer read `permCache` (`service.go:379-380`, `423-424`). So whenever the cached scope map doesn't grant a resource, Check calls `permissionStore.GetUserPermissions` again (`service.go:400`). Only that one exact `(user, action, name, folder)` tuple then goes into the denial cache. Before this change, one DB query per user/action every 30s served every Check, allowed or denied. Now a caller that checks many distinct resources the user can't see (search/list filtering by per-item Check) triggers one permission query per resource. Singleflight only merges calls that run at the same time. You could re-fetch only when the cached entry is older than some threshold, or keep the read-through and invalidate the cache on grant instead.

findings.title: "explicit cache deny" test passes even without the denial cache
findings.body: The comment says the permission cache is set up to *allow* access "to prove this is not checked", but the map value is `false`. So `scopeMap["dashboards:uid:dash1"]` is false and the cached path denies anyway. The DB fallback then uses the default empty `fakeStore` from `setupService` (`service_test.go:1328,1340-1342`), which also denies. The assertion `assert.False(resp.Allowed)` would pass with the denial-cache lookup removed. Set the value to `true` (and/or give the store an allowing permission) so the test fails unless the denial entry short-circuits.

findings.title: `NoopCache` is exported from the `authz` package but only used internally
findings.body: `NoopCache` is used only by `ProvideAuthZClient` (line 103). Exporting it adds public API to `pkg/services/authz`. Make it unexported (`noopCache`), and consider adding `var _ cache.Cache = (*noopCache)(nil)` so the interface conformance is checked at compile time.

contracts.action: Check consults the new per-resource denial cache before anything else
contracts.before_after: Before: one cached scope map per (user, action), so allow and deny were both answered from cache for 30s. After: a hit on the denial key returns deny immediately. A miss checks the cached scope map and returns only on allow; otherwise it queries the DB and writes a denial entry when the result is a deny.
contracts.visible_effect: A user is denied a resource for up to shortCacheTTL after a previous denial. Key collisions (cache.go:31) can deny an unrelated resource.
contracts.failure_mode: Cache Get errors are logged and treated as a miss (cache.go:62-67), so the request falls back to the DB. A Set failure is logged only.

contracts.action: Check/List read cached permissions via new getCachedIdentityPermissions, then fall back to getIdentityPermissions
contracts.equivalent_path: getIdentityPermissions (service.go:320-340), which used to read permCache itself
contracts.before_after: The cached path skips the folders:create action-set expansion, but it uses the same cache key that getUserPermissions writes (service.go:379,406), so it reads the same content. The cache read was removed from getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions, so their DB path always queries the store.
contracts.visible_effect: Allows come from cache. Denials re-query the DB, so new grants show up sooner. Revocations still lag by up to 30s, as before.
contracts.failure_mode: If GetUserIdentifiers fails in the cached path, the error is swallowed and the user is looked up again in getUserPermissions (service.go:374). The second lookup surfaces the error, so there is no silent allow.

contracts.action: In-process authz client switches from a 30s local cache to NoopCache
contracts.before_after: In-process Check/List calls are no longer cached on the client side. Every call goes through the in-proc channel to rbac.Service, which applies its own caching.
contracts.visible_effect: Permission changes show up faster in-process. Per-request cost now depends on the service's caching.
contracts.failure_mode: NoopCache.Get always returns cache.ErrNotFound. Whether authzlib treats that as a plain miss could not be verified from the vendored source.
contracts.open_question: Does authzlib's client treat cache.ErrNotFound from Get as a miss, and ignore Set returning nil without side effects?

summary: The change adds a per-resource denial cache in front of Check and moves permission-cache reads into a new getCachedIdentityPermissions. Cached allows return immediately, and denials re-query the DB. The in-process client's local cache becomes a no-op. Issues found: (1) the denial cache key is ambiguous, because `_`-joined name/folder UIDs can collide and the identity type is left out, which can silently deny an unrelated resource; (2) each new (resource, user) denial now runs a full permission DB query, where before one query per user/action served every Check for 30s; (3) the "explicit cache deny" test sets the perm-cache value to `false`, so it passes even without the denial cache. Minor: `NoopCache` is exported without need.
